summary: npm package ships only a cloaked-redirect phishing HTML page as main
details: Package bcxhdh1kjlopsde@1.0.0 publishes a single file, index.html, declared as the package `main`. The HTML impersonates a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge, fetches an AES-CTR-encrypted value from api.keyval.org using a hardcoded lookup key (`DC7tr9PjVqMIf1EYczH1puouOG21C0khV3VzWnxdtI`), decrypts it in the browser to resolve a destination host, calls `/api/strategies/check?cid=...` on that host, and `window.location.replace`s the visitor to the returned URL. The package name is random and there is no JavaScript entry point, no lifecycle script, and no code that executes on `npm install` or `require()` — HTML is not a JS module, so a developer installing or importing this package is not harmed by its contents. The artifact appears to be a cloaked-redirect / traffic-distribution phishing page using api.keyval.org as an encrypted dead-drop for the destination host, misused as a hosting channel on the npm registry rather than a functioning Node package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
